# Database and archive inventory

## User-provided archive — not copied to GitHub

| Item | Known details |
| --- | --- |
| Name | `ascension-data-main(2).zip` |
| Size | ~420,659,725 bytes (~401 MiB) |
| Entries | 22,678 observed archive entries |
| Provenance | User-shared ChatGPT Library archive |
| Library reference | `libfile_08cbcf4f4dbc819188437e1945f3200c` |
| Share URL | https://chatgpt.com/library/share/libfile_08cbcf4f4dbc819188437e1945f3200c?account_id=personal |
| Status | Link/index recorded **only**; original ZIP was **not uploaded or mirrored to this repository** |

An earlier archive name was `ascension-data-main(1).zip`; version-equivalence and complete content have not been verified. Preserve both labels when tracing changes.

### Why no direct ZIP commit?
GitHub regular Git blobs have a 100 MiB hard file limit, and repository writes here are designed for text. Uploading a >400 MB file requires Git LFS or external artifact storage with appropriate limits; a Library share link may require ChatGPT authentication or later expire.

## Public corpora currently indexed but not mirrored
- https://github.com/Bharph/coa-preservation-data — class spellbook and tooltip preservation; potential referenced external data packs.
- https://github.com/DealsBeam/ascension-db — SQL conversion with 464,048 rows.
- https://github.com/f3rr311/CoA-Databank — coabuildhub/client datamine source material.
- https://github.com/Conquest-of-AzerothCore/azerothcore-wotlk-coa — server and world data (large project).
- https://github.com/Ryansousa10/coa-tier-list/tree/main/tools/data/raw — BisBeard captures.
- https://github.com/kevinvongmany/bisbeard-db — glyph capture.

## Recommended durable preservation
Keep this **index and derived manifests** in CoA-Research; preserve large third-party data as pinned upstream revisions or legally permitted mirrors, with source licenses. Keep user-private game files in private storage. For every large archive, record SHA-256, bytes, source timestamp, license, and extraction script version when available. Do not treat a URL as a verified copy.

# September 2, 2026 spellbook capture extraction

Source: https://github.com/Bharph/coa-preservation-data/blob/main/class-spellbooks/by-class.json

The upstream capture contains all **21** class codes but mostly empty `talents` sections (metadata-only `activeGroup`). The **only class with actual talent tree entries in this extracted file is BARBARIAN**. Its three named saved tabs are Forbidden Arts, Forbearance, and Acuity. Other class specialization names and talent ranks are **not recoverable from this particular field**. The adjacent CSV contains only actual named talent tabs and their linked-node and max-rank counts. Counts are capacities from unspent snapshots, **not chosen builds or power values**.

This is a final-week *client observation* and should not override a verified late-production specialization roster. Obtain the missing trees from upstream client advancement data, the public talent presentation and the changelog; the client advancement baseline was frozen 2026-02-08 and thus requires later overlays.

Conquest restoration priority: parse 2026-08-01 through 2026-08-31 original changelog text, then overlay the 2026-09-02 live tooltip values. All late-server coefficients remain unknown until extracted.

# CoA AscensionLogs — source analysis
Research date: 2026-10-29. Maintainer: Uncle Bone.

## Verified public capabilities
Website: https://coa.ascensionlogs.gg/
FAQ: https://coa.ascensionlogs.gg/faq

- Reports, boss rankings, phase/difficulty statistics, tier lists, actual-player Builds (talents, gear, enchants), character armory, guild progression and Mythic+ rankings are advertised. This does **not** mean a complete historic dataset has been downloaded.
- Companion records otherwise missing WoW 3.3.5a combatant information (gear/talents), supplemented via raid inspect and character-specific Ascension APIs.
- The site explicitly describes combat attribution, boss-specific damage rules (whitelist, blacklist, target caps, excluded spells), snapshot parses and per-encounter specialization detection.
- Rankings rebuild about every 30 minutes; Mythic+ Ascension leaderboard polling about hourly. Observed runs and uploaded captures may differ in timing/completeness.
- Spec parses use the matching class+spec/boss/bracket/difficulty/phase cohort. Class parses aggregate by class. All Star per-boss score = 100*(best DPS / top DPS)^0.95, summed across bosses in a zone.
- Class identification uses unambiguous spell indicators; spec identification uses prioritized per-encounter spell event matching. The live indicator matrix sometimes fails to render to public browsers.
- Tank tagging requires a qualifying tank specialization and >=20% share of tank-targeted damage by the site's methodology.
- Absorbs must be inferred on 3.3.5a because explicit absorb events are absent; comparisons to Details! need caution.
- The FAQ states free API keys can be generated in Profile Settings; API supports aggregate statistics. Attribution to CoA Logs is required for public display; bulk dataset redistribution is forbidden. Prefer permitted API access rather than scraping.

## Third-party existing capture, with independent provenance
https://github.com/Ryansousa10/coa-tier-list
- README documents https://coa.ascensionlogs.gg/api/statistics plus class-specs and phases endpoints; phase/difficulty/role combinations, bossId, damageMode and rankings.
- Raw captures in tools/data/raw (verified GitHub directory listing on 2026-10-29): ascensionlogs-data.json (995,595 bytes), ascensionlogs-data2.json (2 bytes — **do not consider usable**), boss-stats-raw.json (343,642 bytes), bosses-meta.json (3,789 bytes), mythic-plus-raw.json (2,415,508 bytes), rankings-raw.json (894,678 bytes), tank-focus-raw.json (540 bytes). File existence/size does NOT imply validity or complete history.
- Capture scripts: tools/scrape/ascension-logs.mjs, rankings.mjs, mythic-plus.mjs, healer-tank-focus.mjs, sanity-check.mjs.
- The project's tiers are **their own formula**, not official logs ratings: median (or p95 in top mode), normalized to highest spec; S>=85%, A>=68%, B>=50%, C>=32%, D otherwise; fewer than 5 parses flagged. They use boss-only/trash modes when data exists.
- The README warns that healing HPS queries omit role=healer, and Cloudflare can block server-side HTTP access.

## Companion technical reference
https://github.com/FangYuanWoW/AscensionLogsCompanion
An accessible public README describes background inspection of raid equipment/talents, compression, chunking and embedding of custom snapshots in combat logs for the service to parse. Check license and exact deployed version before copying code. Do not reproduce another service's event protocol without consent.

## Validation gaps / next tasks
1. Obtain authorized developer API documentation and characterize endpoints, pagination, phase ID, and aggregation scope. Do not publish credentials.
2. Record timestamps, realm, phase, boss, difficulty, sample size, role, damage mode, and upstream revision for each statistic.
3. Independently compare extracts against the live site and known combat logs; reject 2-byte/empty results.
4. Identify old phases whose records remain accessible; do not assert complete historic logs without enumeration.
5. Respect attribution and prohibition on bulk redistribution; store methods, links, schemas and authorized small examples only.

## Potential addon use
Details! — guardian owner and absorb edge cases; DBM-CoA/MRT — encounter classification; BoneBiS — observed player builds as corroborating evidence, not proof of theoretical optimality; BoneBuilds — talent popularity, with encounter/sample filters.

# BisBeard CoA — recovered dataset provenance
Research date: 2026-10-29. Maintainer: Uncle Bone.

Original CoA endpoint: https://coa.bisbeard.com/
Other endpoint described by a third-party project: https://gear-planner-api.bisbeard.workers.dev/api/data/manifest?reader=2
Availability of either endpoint is unverified today. Historical snapshots exist in third-party GitHub; do not claim full all-phase BiS completion.

## Verified public GitHub file listing
Source: https://github.com/Ryansousa10/coa-tier-list/tree/main/tools/data/raw
- bisbeard-meta.json — 33,873 bytes; repository README describes CoA classes/specs, defaultWeights, roles and equippable armor/weapon constraints.
- bisbeard-items-p1.json — 18,457,734 bytes; README describes Phase 1 items.
- bisbeard-items-p2.json — 8,069,215 bytes; existence verified, coverage and semantics NOT yet checked.
These are upstream snapshots rather than validated current-client authoritative datasets. Keep original authorship and license restrictions.

Extraction source: https://github.com/Ryansousa10/coa-tier-list/blob/main/tools/scrape/bisbeard.mjs
Build algorithm: https://github.com/Ryansousa10/coa-tier-list/blob/main/tools/build-data.mjs
Upstream README: https://github.com/Ryansousa10/coa-tier-list/blob/main/README.md

The third-party optimizer ranks items with sum(item_stat * spec_weight) plus parsed weapon DPS, applying equipment eligibility, excluding PvP/Bloodforged candidates and grouping item variants. This is a stat-weighted approximation, **not** a verified global optimum. Effects, set bonuses, hit/haste caps, procs, rotational effects and real encounter lengths can reverse an item order.

Other preservation leads: https://github.com/kevinvongmany/bisbeard-db (glyphs_ascension.ts), https://github.com/Leemo94/BisBuddy. See research/BISBEARD.md for more.

## Recommended structured research rows
Each BiS candidate: realm/client build, phase, class, specialization, role, slot, item ID, item variant, source/drop, stat weights version, formula, restrictions, publication timestamp, validation status, and upstream URL. Never conflate highest parse wearing an item with causation.

## Coverage assessment
- Phase 1: third-party item snapshot confirmed present.
- Phase 2: separate snapshot confirmed present, **not validated for completeness**.
- Phase 3 onward: not found in inspected raw directory.
- All classes/specs across all phases: **not verified**.
- No copies of large third-party datasets committed here: licensing, attribution and permissible redistribution require review first.

# Historical CoA BisBeard preservation

The old Conquest of Azeroth BisBeard endpoint was **https://coa.bisbeard.com/**. Availability is unreliable or discontinued; avoid asserting a complete backup exists.

## Recovered references
- [CoA tier list historical data](https://github.com/Ryansousa10/coa-tier-list/tree/main/tools/data/raw):
  - `bisbeard-meta.json` — observed file approximately 33,873 bytes; contains metadata from historical BisBeard capture.
  - `bisbeard-items-p1.json` — observed approximately 18,457,734 bytes.
  - `bisbeard-items-p2.json` — observed approximately 8,069,215 bytes.
  - Additional rankings, boss stats, Mythic+ and other captures available in that folder.
- [BisBeard source scraper](https://github.com/Ryansousa10/coa-tier-list/blob/main/tools/scrape/bisbeard.mjs) — request/extraction code to document provenance.
- [BisBeard glyph archive](https://github.com/kevinvongmany/bisbeard-db) — `glyphs_ascension.ts`, observed around 509 KB.
- [BisBuddy](https://github.com/Leemo94/BisBuddy) — related reference.
- [BisBeard root](https://bisbeard.com/) — independent availability from discontinued CoA subdomain.

Preserved item rankings, stat weights, and glyph data help gear/talent guides. They **do not** establish live spell IDs, simulation accuracy, or current phase BiS without version comparisons. The user prefers useful historical data even without a guarantee of present-day currency, so retain date/provenance rather than discarding it.

# BoneArchive platform scope and provenance

The public GitHub Pages site is static. It cannot receive, authenticate, store, index or publicly share user-uploaded logs. The first log explorer reads a selected text log locally in the browser, summarizes event types and candidate ability casts, and exports JSON. It is **not** an upload backend, historical report browser, full parser, or boss encounter analyzer. Public uploads require a separate secure service with authentication, explicit consent, moderation, retention policy, abuse controls, storage and processing costs.

## Planned research-backed sections

1. Original Bisbeard-like gear planner: item source/license audit, phase/class/spec catalog, eligibility, sockets, sets, stats, enchants, caps, source-attributed reconstructed sets and explicit original BiS when recovered.
2. Ascension Logs-like report explorer: links to legitimately accessible historical reports, locally analyzed logs, normalized encounter timelines, comparisons and a separately deployed upload service when ready.
3. Meta and tier browser: only rankings tied to metric, difficulty, phase, sample size, snapshot and methodology. No fake S/A/B rankings.
4. Talents and builds: versioned tree references and observed build evidence; avoid presenting theorycrafted recommendations as historical fact.
5. DBM research: combat event schema, source GUID/NPC identification, ability IDs, cast intervals, phases and confidence per encounter; corroborate multiple pulls.

## Third-party rules

CoA Logs FAQ https://coa.ascensionlogs.gg/faq permits public API use with attribution but forbids bulk redistribution. Use its API with permission and do not republish entire historical datasets. Public code and datasets have their own licenses; no blanket copying of Bisbeard or Ascension Sidekick assets or designs. Sidekick is an inspiration for *feature categories*, not source code or visual design.

## Log parser caveats

WoW 3.3.5 combat logs vary in prefixes, quoted fields and expansion-specific events. The initial browser analyzer is deliberately a rough local event summary; it does not correctly attribute all combat mechanics, infer absorb amounts, group encounters, identify pets, or calculate DPS/HPS. Validate any DBM timer against multiple complete pulls and client logs before using it.

# Engineering plan — historical gear and logs intelligence
Updated 2026-10-29.

Goal: use BisBeard stat-weighted candidates and CoA AscensionLogs performance/build evidence without confusing the two.

1. Inventory raw snapshots and upstream licenses. Record SHA-256, retrieval time and Git commit; inspect Phase 2 schema separately from Phase 1.
2. Map phase identifiers, realm aliases, class/spec spelling, item variants and IDs against https://ascension-db.ascension-archive.workers.dev/ and https://coa-development.org/talents.
3. Normalize rows in a separate *research* dataset (never preload megabytes into a 3.3.5a addon). Require clear phase/class/spec/slot keys and provenance.
4. Calculate stat-weight candidate score and document unsupported effects (procs, sets, breakpoints, custom mechanics).
5. Query supported, authorized aggregate AscensionLogs data for observed equipment/talent patterns, retaining boss, phase, difficulty, percentile and sample-size metadata.
6. Publish only permitted curated/derived content with proper attribution, never bulk copy the logs API dataset. A Windows companion or external build step can perform authorized sync; WoW 3.3.5a Lua cannot directly fetch arbitrary HTTPS APIs.
7. Validate with actual Conquest Reborn behavior, tooltips and combat records. Mark statuses: verified-live, corroborated, historical, inferred, incomplete.
8. Deliver lightweight per-phase Lua tables or links to externally maintained guides; guard memory and SavedVariables growth.

Research links:
- https://github.com/Ryansousa10/coa-tier-list
- https://coa.ascensionlogs.gg/faq

# Combat meter and addon development notes

## Target
Ascension Conquest Reborn, WoW 3.3.5a-based client. All classes and specs; vanilla/TBC/WotLK/custom content. Respect base UI, DragonUI and ElvUI. Full UI replacements such as BoneUI can be standalone.

## Details! CoA — priority bugs
- **Combat history loss:** Segments reportedly vanished when zoning, leaving instances (e.g. Headless Horseman), reloading, or fighting a new trash/boss segment. Check segment cleanup, instance transitions, `IsTrash()` filtering, saved segment limit and SavedVariables load path. Do not claim reliable persistence without in-game validation.
- **Pet names / ownership:** Unknown pet names and damage credited incorrectly. Handle `SPELL_SUMMON` source+destination GUID pairs, `UNIT_PET` when possible, guardian/turret events, nil GUIDs, a cached GUID->name->owner relationship, and noisy combat-log name fallbacks. Preserve actual pet ownership rather than reassigning unknowns to an arbitrary actor.
- **Tinker:** Mechanics, Invention and Demolition plus engineering guardians, constructs and periodic effects. Spell mapping requires client evidence.
- **DPS/HPS correctness:** Separate direct damage, pet damage, heals, absorbs and periodic damage. Avoid double-counting or phantom owner attribution.
- **Version:** Earlier local build `Details-CoA-v1.0.3-TEST.zip` was archive integrity checked but **not in-game validated**. That ZIP was a ChatGPT conversation artifact, **not stored in this repo**. The user's [Details repository](https://github.com/uncle-bone/Details) previously had documentation but not the entire source.

## Client limitations and known errors
- 3.3.5a APIs differ from Retail. Modern `GetCurrentEnvironment`, `CreateVector2D` and libraries relying on them may be unavailable.
- Do not assume stock 3.3.5a spellbook frame/UI when DragonUI or ElvUI changes the visual layer. Scan client spell APIs where supported; use event-driven discovery for truly custom abilities.
- A reliable sharing channel architecture: Questie-X, LootCollector and DBM-CoA share LootCollector's existing default global channel, distinguish messages with separate addon prefixes/protocols, and should not each create or join new channels.
- Keep code modular and memory efficient. Lazy-load optional reference data; avoid full SQL/DBC dumps in Lua.
- Preserve third-party license notices; maintainer branding is **Uncle Bone**, contact https://github.com/uncle-bone.
- Create Discord-ready release notes for addon updates (under 2,000 characters) ending exactly `:dragon: Uncle Bone :dragon:`.

## Source leads
- [Details repository](https://github.com/uncle-bone/Details)
- [CoA AzerothCore](https://github.com/Conquest-of-AzerothCore/azerothcore-wotlk-coa)
- [CoAAnalytics](https://github.com/265ada/CoAAnalytics)
- [Community MRT](https://github.com/ArgonautCaptain/Method-Raid-Tools-Ascension-CoA)
- [CoA preservation](https://github.com/Bharph/coa-preservation-data)

# Ascension CoA final-balance restoration — research baseline

Maintainer: Uncle Bone (@uncle-bone). Initiated 2026-10-29.

## Mission and target
Reconstruct the balance state of the original Ascension Conquest of Azeroth (CoA) realms immediately before the reported early-September 2026 shutdown, for implementation and validation in Conquest Reborn. **Do not confuse a community emulator's current data, an old frozen client snapshot, a tier list, or a historical patch announcement with the final server-side live values.**

Official marketing advertised 21 classes / 69 specializations in June 2025, but an August 2026 community roster describes about 70 builds and fourth specializations. The exact final roster is **not yet verified**. Build an authoritative per-class/spec manifest before claiming complete coverage.

## Most promising surviving contemporaneous evidence
1. [Bharph/coa-preservation-data](https://github.com/Bharph/coa-preservation-data): repository describes **70,437 Ascension API changelog entries from 2016-07-23 through 2026-08-31**, fetched 2026-09-02; **~180,282 spell tooltip records** captured in-game; 21 class spellbooks captured **2026-09-02**; client `CharacterAdvancementData.json` containing 23,709 nodes but **frozen 2026-02-08**; and spell ranks. **These are source-reported corpus sizes, not independently audited totals in this project.** Many class spellbooks only show starter spells; the fourth-spec graphs may have remained server-side.
2. [AscensionLogs CoA](https://coa.ascensionlogs.gg/): historic report/performance evidence where available, not an exported snapshot of all tuning. See [ASCENSIONLOGS.md](ASCENSIONLOGS.md); follow usage terms and avoid bulk reproduction.
3. [Ry an Sousa tier-list capture](https://github.com/Ryansousa10/coa-tier-list) (remove space in project slug: `Ryansousa10`): source-reported statistics and ranking snapshots, with non-official tier calculations; preserve phase, boss, date, parse counts and provenance.
4. [Kami Labs CoA patch-note catalog](https://kami-labs.fr/en/patch-notes-ascension/): accessible secondary recap of substantial Aug 2026 tuning waves on Aug 1, 8, 15, 20, 23, 26. Always verify specific figures against the raw archived Ascension changelog.
5. [DealsBeam/ascension-db](https://github.com/DealsBeam/ascension-db), [CoA Databank](https://github.com/f3rr311/CoA-Databank), [CoA AzerothCore](https://github.com/Conquest-of-AzerothCore/azerothcore-wotlk-coa), and [CoA talent reference](https://coa-development.org/talents): cross-check spell IDs, talent graphs, implementation clues; never assume they reproduce original live coefficients.
6. [CoA arena extractor](https://github.com/johnayoung/coa-arena): client-extracted ability references / healer and DPS heuristics; check snapshot date and algorithm before use.

## Specific late-stage changes that must not be omitted
- July 31–Aug 1: 21-class balance pass and Fierce Blows absorb/block interaction change (secondary recap: https://kami-labs.fr/en/ascension/patch-zul-gurub-ascension-coa-21-classes-remaniees/).
- Aug 6–8: Templar oath-chain rework, PvE monster-damage bonuses for individual specializations (secondary recap: https://kami-labs.fr/en/ascension/patch-ascension-coa-refonte-templier-molten-core/).
- Aug 9–15: Runemaster Weapon Engraving rework, multi-class buffs (https://kami-labs.fr/en/ascension/patch-ascension-coa-refonte-maitre-des-runes/).
- Aug 15–20: Sun Cleric Blessings / Starcaller Moon Priest healer revisions; reported +20% base health for CoA classes and resilience changes (https://kami-labs.fr/en/ascension/patch-ascension-coa-refonte-soigneurs-jcj/).
- Aug 20–22: Stormbringer/Felsworn offensive revisions and PvP adjustments; secondary article distinguishes changes active at publication from **restart-pending** changes (https://kami-labs.fr/en/ascension/patch-ascension-coa-porte-tempete-gangrelie/).
- Aug 26: Witch Hunter rework listed at https://kami-labs.fr/en/patch-notes-ascension/ . Verify all changes through Aug 31 directly.

## Evidence grades for reconstruction
- **A — Confirmed final:** original late-live server data or two independently corroborating late-live measurements fixing the exact effective value, with timestamp and rules.
- **B — Contemporaneous direct:** original Aug/Sep 2026 changelog, client tooltip, in-game snapshot or authentic log; implementation state and server-side overrides may still be uncertain.
- **C — Indirect:** third-party summary, client-derived conversion, archived rankings or emulator source with unverified final parity.
- **D — Hypothesis:** extrapolated/inferred value, needing testing. No guesses labeled original.
- **Unknown:** blank rather than imputed zero.

Each restoration record needs: class, specialization, stable spell/talent ID, name, rank, mechanic, exact value/formula, source URL/path and row or message ID, source capture date, patch effective date, realm, PvE/PvP mode, applicability, whether restart-pending, confidence grade, and a Conquest Reborn test case.

## First implementation deliverable for Conquest
A reproducible **final-value ledger**, not a generic tier list. Extract, filter and order the original changelog by effective date; link each affected spell ID to tooltip/rank/talent evidence; identify per-spec server overrides; compare with Conquest Reborn implementation; publish exact mismatch and fix recommendation only where sufficiently supported. Maintain separate PvE and PvP baselines and report sample sizes for log-derived performance.

# Ordered final-balance recovery workflow

1. **Freeze the snapshot:** target original CoA's last live state around early September 2026; establish exact shutdown and last applied restart timestamps from primary records before specifying an authoritative cutoff.

7. **Deliver implementation packet:** per-class/spec ledger, confirmed mismatch, supporting primary citations, suggested SQL/C++/script change point, reproducible test with expected output, and uncertainty register.

# Historical CoA meta and BiS reconstruction methodology
Maintainer: Uncle Bone. Updated 2026-10-29.

## Metrics
DPS and HPS per boss/phase/difficulty, median and 95th percentile when available, number of parses, encounter duration and date; Mythic+ key and run context separately. Track spec and class separately. A highest parse is not a representative ranking. Never mix all-damage with boss-only DPS or healing with damage.

## Tier lists
Each published tier requires exact formula, source snapshots, phase, difficulty, metric, date window and sample size. Label custom percentile thresholds as community-derived, not official Ascension tier ratings. Prefer minimum sample threshold and confidence bands where possible.

## BiS
Distinguish (a) original BisBeard published saved set, (b) reconstructed stat-weight candidates, (c) observed high-performing player gear, (d) simulated/verified optimal sets. Model armor/weapon eligibility, uniqueness, sockets, enchants, caps, procs, sets, talents, glyphs, tinkers and encounter-specific effects. Linear weights alone cannot prove BiS.

## Provenance
Keep original source URL, Git commit/hash, observed file checksum, capture timestamp if present, realm, class/spec identifiers, phase labels, and evidence status. No invented stats or items. Never expose private logs or identifiers; honor source licensing and API terms.

# Spell, class, and specialization research

## Data hierarchy
1. **Observed Conquest Reborn client data and combat logs:** highest priority for actual spell IDs, class/spec behavior and combat-log encoding.
2. **Client DBC/WDB and verified extracts:** strong candidates; record client version, timestamp and source files.
3. **Preserved class spellbooks/tooltips:** broad historical coverage, not necessarily exact current spell effects.
4. **CoA AzerothCore and SQL mirrors:** useful names, ranks, NPCs, spell code and possible effect IDs. Do not assume exact parity with Ascension live realm.
5. **CoA talent calculators / BisBeard metadata:** cross-check names, roles, builds and relationships; cannot prove combat-log effects alone.

## Known corpus
- [DealsBeam/ascension-db](https://github.com/DealsBeam/ascension-db) README states **464,048 SQL rows across seven files**, derived from an August 2026 preservation snapshot. Spell-oriented SQL contains **222,456 rows** including `spell_dbc` + `spell_ranks`. This figure **is not 222,456 unique playable class abilities**.
- The same audit [missing.md](https://github.com/DealsBeam/ascension-db/blob/main/missing.md) documents lost raw DBC attributes, proc flags, numeric spell-effect fields, and other missing information. Never invent them.
- [CoA preservation](https://github.com/Bharph/coa-preservation-data) contains class spellbooks, spell tooltips, caches and changelogs; manifests can point to data packs not bundled in the base archive. Confirm pack acquisition before claiming the corpus is wholly imported.
- [CoA Databank](https://github.com/f3rr311/CoA-Databank), [talent scraper](https://github.com/v1cferr/ascension-coa-scraper), and [CoA talents site](https://coa-development.org/talents) provide complementary class/talent sources.
- [CoA AzerothCore](https://github.com/Conquest-of-AzerothCore/azerothcore-wotlk-coa) has `modules/mod-spellbook`, `modules/mod-ascension` and `data/coa-world`; the project's SQL and modules should be inspected selectively for relevant mappings.

## Important caveats
- A Tinker-related SQL completion patch was **reported missing** from the DealsBeam conversion baseline (`rev_20260910_15_tinker_completion.sql`). Consult upstream/release archives; do not assume Tinker coverage complete.
- Tinker specialization terminology includes **Mechanics, Invention, Demolition** in the user's development scope; IDs 49/50/51 are **candidate mappings requiring verification**, not an authoritative API guarantee.
- Vanilla, TBC and WotLK spell references are all in development scope, even when expansion gameplay is not currently accessible.
- Many effects arrive as separate aura/periodic/summon events rather than the player's direct attack. A spell-ID lookup is insufficient to identify ownership.

## Future import format
Create an extracted, versioned `CSV/JSON` manifest with `spell_id, name, rank, source, source_version, class, specialization, category, confidence`, separate from small runtime Lua lookup tables. Annotate uncertain fields. Preserve third-party licenses and provenance.

Avoid forcing hundreds of thousands of rows into a game addon at startup. Use minimal tables for exceptions and rely on client `GetSpellInfo` when available.

# BiS candidate eligibility audit — October 30, 2026

## Scope and method

Audited all 140 preserved Phase 1 and Phase 2 specialization files: 70 specialization profiles in each phase. Files come from `Ryansousa10/coa-tier-list/public/data/bis/`, pinned by the source index to commit `92616fe829e79335e8bdc6139c7ceb7619b4d63a`. Candidate armor and weapons were compared with BoneArchive's preserved `site/data/equipment-rules.json`, including class armor and weapon permissions, spec-specific ranged weapon restrictions, one- and two-hand restrictions, shield eligibility, and dual-wield rules. Rules whose metadata names a required talent are reported as conditional rather than generally eligible.

The audit also compared every file's embedded weight map against its matching profile in `site/weights.js`. The local source index and class/spec roster map the 140 files to all 70 specializations.

## Results

- All 140 files were fetched and parsed; no source files failed.
- All 140 embedded weight maps match the corresponding local specialization profile exactly. This verifies data consistency with the historical BisBeard profiles, not that those weights are optimal for every build or encounter.
- 65 candidate rows conflict with the preserved class/spec eligibility rules; the gear page now filters them from selectable candidates.
- One additional shield candidate is talent-gated and remains visible with its required node ID.

| Finding | Rows | Scope |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Wand candidates in Bow/Crossbow-only ranged slots | 24 | Witch Doctor — Shadowhunting and Starcaller — Sentinel; all six candidates in each phase for both specs |
| Shield candidates disallowed by the class equipment record | 14 | Barbarian — Brutality; Bloodmage — Fleshweaver; Chronomancer — Artificer; Felsworn — Tyrant; Pyromancer — Flameweaving; Reaper — Domination; Templar — Oathkeeper; Venomancer — Fortitude; Witch Hunter — Black Knight |
| One-handed maces barred by class rules | 18 | Bloodmage — Accursed/Eternal; Felsworn — Slayer/Tyrant; Reaper — Soul/Harvest/Domination; Witch Hunter — Black Knight/Inquisition |
| Off-hand weapons conflicting with specialization dual-wield rules | 9 | Barbarian — Brutality (three swords; dagger exceptions remain allowed); Bloodmage — Accursed (two); Witch Hunter — Black Knight (four) |
| Shield requiring a specific talent | 1 conditional | Barbarian — Ancestry; talent node `31219` |

For the two ranged specs, the saved six-item candidates for each phase are all wands. No eligible bow or crossbow replacement appears in those spec files, so the page reports the slot as having no preserved eligible candidate instead of substituting a guess.

## Limitations and interpretation

`equipment-rules.json` is extracted from the same preserved BisBeard metadata (`site/data/remote.json` points to the corresponding source commit). It is a strong internal consistency check, but it is not an independently validated live-client proficiency database. Historical weights are weighted-score inputs, not combat simulations or proof of best-in-slot. The upstream snapshots contain up to six candidates per slot, so removing an invalid row may leave fewer than six valid alternatives. A full replacement ranking needs the complete phase item pool and should retain the same eligibility filters.

The original item candidate data remains unchanged upstream. BoneArchive applies the eligibility checks when rendering the list and documents this audit in its research catalog.
